text: Moesha (/moʊˈiːʃə/, MOH-EE-shə) is an American television sitcom that aired on UPN from January 23, 1996, to May 14, 2001. The series stars R&B singer Brandy as Moesha Denise Mitchell, an African-American teenager living with her upper middle class family in the Leimert Park neighborhood of Los Angeles. It was originally ordered as a pilot for CBS' 1995–1996 television season but was declined by the network; it was later picked up by UPN, which aired it as a mid-season replacement. It became the biggest success for the nascent network and one of the greatest hits during UPN's entire run. The series was a joint production for UPN by Regan Jon Productions, Saradipity Productions, and Jump at the Sun Productions in association with Big Ticket Television. The show centers on the life of a black upper-middle-class family through the eyes of Moesha, whose father Frank, a widower and Saturn car salesman (and later owner of his own dealership, Brothers Saturn), marries Dee, the vice principal at Moesha's high school, a move that upsets Moesha. The series was created by Ralph Farquhar, along with the writing team of Sara V. Finney and Vida Spears. The settings include the Mitchell household, teen hangout The Den, and Crenshaw High School, where Moesha, Kim, Niecy, and Hakeem attend. The sitcom was set in the Leimert Park neighborhood of Los Angeles and addressed real social issues affecting teenagers, such as premarital sex, the death of a parent, teen pregnancy, drug use, race relations, sexuality, dementia, and day-to-day challenges like gender prejudice and inequality. In the controversial episode "Secrets and Lies" (aired February 7, 2000), the Mitchell family learns from Aunt Hattie that Frank is the biological father of Dorian, whom they and Dorian believed to be Frank's nephew, shocking the family and leading to Dorian's rebellion, Moesha moving out of the home into a dorm room. Moesha was also the first Black-cast sitcom to have an episode devoted to teenagers and non-heterosexuality, "Labels" (aired October 1, 1996), which features Hakeem's cousin Omar arriving at the Mitchell home, causing family fears he might be another Hakeem; Omar turns out to be nice and responsible. Moesha, still grieving her breakup with Q, goes on a date with Omar. After attending a movie, they meet Omar's friend Tracy, leading Moesha to believe Omar may be gay. She shares her suspicions with Kim and Niecy, and soon the school is aware of the rumor. When Hakeem hears the news, Moesha realizes she may have damaged their friendship. The show had different versions of its opening credits theme song, performed by Brandy: a first version for season 1, a second for seasons 2 and 3, and a third for the final three seasons. Although the same recording was used in the last three seasons, two different openings were used for each of the first three. The season 1 opening shows Moesha dancing in front of a fountain, walking with friends, dancing in a moving car, and winning at chess while waving at a guy as he walks away. Seasons 2 and 3 feature Moesha dancing in front of the fountain with a bass guitar player behind her, playing basketball and baseball with friends and family, driving with friends, strutting down a block with Kim and Niecy, teaching Kim how to rollerblade (later replaced with footage of Moesha and Q chasing Myles), and being served a meal at a diner by Andell while seated with her family. When Moesha is distracted by a cute guy, Frank covers her eyes. Season 4 shows the cast around the neighborhood and Moesha, Kim, and Niecy dancing at the fountain in red outfits. Season 5 features the cast dancing in a panoramic view as Norwood lip-syncs to the theme song over a background of clouds and a rising sun. Season 6's opening is similar to season 5 but includes a twist: since Yvette Wilson left to join The Parkers and Sheryl Lee Ralph's character Dee became a recurring character, the opening features Norwood lip-syncing over the portion where Yvette and Sheryl appeared in the prior season's intro. Countess Vaughn left the show in 1999 for her spin-off, The Parkers, which premiered on August 30, 1999, on UPN, centering on Kim attending community college with her mother, played by Mo'Nique. Yvette Wilson joined The Parkers as Andell Wilkerson, Nikki's childhood friend. Several Moesha cast members, including Brandy Norwood, William Allen Young, Shar Jackson, Sheryl Lee Ralph, and Marcus T. Paulk, made crossover appearances on The Parkers, with Lamont Bentley appearing in three episodes. Though not a direct spin-off, Girlfriends was created by Moesha writer Mara Brock Akil and exists in the same universe as Moesha. Maya Wilkes (Golden Brooks) from Girlfriends lives in Leimert Park like the Moesha characters and appeared in an episode babysitting for her sister-in-law Barbara Lee, who is Dorian's birth mother. Niecy appeared in a season 1 episode of Girlfriends. The CW series The Game was spun off from Girlfriends, with Melanie Barnett (Tia Mowry) being a cousin of Girlfriends' main character Joan Clayton (Tracee Ellis Ross); the Melanie and Derwin characters reappeared in the Girlfriends Season 7 finale at Joan's engagement party. On Moesha, Brandy played herself as a celebrity doppelganger to Moesha, and ironically joined The Game in its fifth season as Chardonnay Pitts, further complicating the idea of the show existing in the same universe. By the sixth season, ratings had dropped, and UPN chose not to renew or air a seventh season. The series ended on an unresolved cliffhanger with Myles being kidnapped by a rival of Dorian, Moesha considering moving in with Hakeem or her best friend Niecy, and a positive pregnancy test found in the trash at Moesha's dorm room without identification. Entertainment Weekly reported a rumor that certain plots would be resolved on The Parkers, but those storylines were never resolved. On November 3, 2017, the cast reunited on The Real and expressed interest in reviving the show, with Norwood stating, "Absolutely, we need a reboot to this show, because we ended on a cliffhanger." In August 2020, Norwood revealed she was in talks for a reboot, citing the show's success on Netflix. The show aired in syndication on UPN, Fox, and The WB affiliates, and on WGN America (now NewsNation) from 2005 to 2008, The N from 2005 to 2009, Up TV, BET Her, and BET until mid-2016, Fuse until 2019, Bounce TV until 2021, and currently airs on Dabl since 2023. On Up TV, it was edited for content to be more "family-friendly," and was heavily edited on BET and BET Her due to airtime constraints. In the UK, Moesha aired on Channel 4 from 1996 to 1998, with only the first three seasons broadcast, and on Nickelodeon from 1996 to 2000, showing only the first four seasons edited for children's television. Paramount Channel aired it from 2000 to 2003, and Trouble from 2003 to 2006. From November 1, 2019, the show began airing on Trace Vault following its rebrand from The Vault. Since 2008, the show has aired in international syndication in Spain, Portugal, Israel, the Middle East, Russia, France, Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Belgium, Ireland, South Africa, Latin America, Brazil, and Australia. In Spain, it aired on Disney Channel from 2005 to 2011 in an edited format suitable for children's television. In Italy, it currently airs on Canale 8. The series is currently streaming on Netflix in the US, with The Parkers also available on the platform. It is also available on Paramount+, BET+, and Hulu. On September 27, 2011, CBS Home Entertainment released Moesha: The First Season on DVD in Region 1 via Amazon.com's CreateSpace program, a Manufacture-on-Demand (MOD) release available exclusively through Amazon.com.
